response.text:
I can do that — but because removing mail is destructive I need a quick confirmation before I run anything.

Here’s the sensible default I propose:
- Action: delete (move to Trash) all conversations with the label "Newsletters" older than 12 months from today.
- Exclusions: keep starred conversations (so anything you’ve flagged stays).
- Consequence: deleted items go to Gmail Trash and are permanently removed after 30 days (you can restore from Trash during that window).

If you prefer a less-destructive option, I can archive instead (removes them from Inbox/labels but keeps them in your account), or I can change the cutoff (e.g., 9/18 months) or *also* preserve messages marked Important.

Please reply with one clear choice:
- “Delete — 12 months — keep starred” (my recommended default), or
- “Archive — 12 months,” or
- “Delete — 18 months — keep starred and important,” or
- Give any other specific cutoff/action/exclusions you want.

Once you confirm, I’ll proceed.
